english: to occur, to happen, to arise
usage: 문제가 발생했어요.
A problem occurred.
발생하다 = (a problem/event) comes into being. The thing that occurs takes 이/가, never 을/를. More formal than 생기다.
사고가 발생한 시간을 알 수 있을까요?
Could I know the time the accident happened?
Common in reports and notices — 사고가/화재가/오류가 발생하다 (an accident/fire/error occurs).
examples: 결제 중에 오류가 발생했습니다.
An error occurred during payment.
발생했습니다 (formal) is the standard wording you see on screens and official notices.
추가 비용이 발생할 수 있어요.
Additional charges may be incurred.
비용이 발생하다 = a cost arises — set phrase for fees and surcharges.
문제가 발생하면 바로 알려 주세요.
If a problem comes up, please let me know right away.
Conditional 발생하면 is everyday phrasing; a notch more formal than 생기면.
nuance: 발생하다 is a formal, written-leaning verb for an event, problem, or phenomenon coming into existence — accidents, errors, fires, costs, diseases. It is intransitive: the thing that occurs takes 이/가, so you can't 'occur something.' In casual speech Koreans often say 생기다 instead (문제가 생겼어요), but 발생하다 is the word for news, reports, manuals, and official announcements.
mistakes: Don't use it transitively — say 문제가 발생했어요 (a problem occurred), not 문제를 발생했어요.
Writing 발생하요 instead of 발생해요 — 하다 always contracts to 해요.

usage: 그런 방법은 존재하지 않아요.
Such a method doesn't exist.
존재하다 = to exist (as a concept/thing). The negative 존재하지 않아요 is the natural way to say 'there's no such thing.'
완벽한 사람은 존재하지 않아요.
A perfect person doesn't exist.
존재하다 is more abstract and emphatic than 있다 — it stresses the very existence of something.
examples: 우주에 생명체가 존재할까요?
Does life exist in the universe?
존재할까요? = a thoughtful 'does it exist?' — used for big, abstract questions.
그 문제는 오래전부터 존재했어요.
That problem has existed for a long time.
For long-standing issues; 존재했어요 stresses that it has 'been there' all along.
편견은 여전히 사회에 존재합니다.
Prejudice still exists in society.
Formal 존재합니다 fits essays and serious discussion about society.
nuance: 존재하다 means 'to exist' in an abstract or emphatic sense, common in writing, debate, and serious topics. For everyday 'there is / I have,' Koreans use 있다 (책이 있어요), not 존재하다. Reach for 존재하다 when you want to stress the very existence of something — a method, a being, a problem — or to deny it flatly with 존재하지 않아요. It is intransitive; the thing that exists takes 이/가.
mistakes: Don't replace everyday 있다 with 존재하다 — 'I have a question' is 질문이 있어요, not 질문이 존재해요.
The natural negative is 존재하지 않아요; '존재 안 해요' sounds clipped and off-register for this abstract verb.

english: to develop, to advance, to progress
usage: 기술이 빠르게 발전하고 있어요.
Technology is developing fast.
발전하다 = to grow and advance to a higher level. The thing that develops takes 이/가 (intransitive).
두 사람의 관계가 연인으로 발전했어요.
The two people's relationship developed into a romance.
~(으)로 발전하다 = 'develop INTO': 연인으로, 큰 문제로, 사업으로.
examples: 그 도시는 빠르게 발전했어요.
That city developed rapidly.
For cities, economies, industries growing — 도시가/경제가 발전하다.
꾸준히 하면 실력이 발전할 거예요.
If you keep at it, your skills will improve.
실력이 발전하다 = one's skills advance — encouraging line about progress.
작은 다툼이 큰 싸움으로 발전했어요.
A small spat developed into a big fight.
Note: 발전하다 can also mean a situation escalates INTO something bigger (often negative).
nuance: 발전하다 means to move to a more advanced, mature, or larger stage — used for technology, economies, skills, and relationships. It's usually intransitive (실력이 발전하다), and the 'into' target takes ~(으)로 (연인으로 발전하다). Don't confuse it with 발견하다 (to discover), which looks similar but is unrelated. For making something better on purpose, the transitive partner is 발전시키다 (경제를 발전시키다).
mistakes: Don't mix up 발전하다 (develop/advance) with 발견하다 (discover) — one syllable apart, totally different meanings.
To say 'develop X' transitively, use 발전시키다: 기술을 발전시켰어요, not 기술을 발전했어요.

english: to be improved, to be enhanced
usage: 듣기 실력이 많이 향상됐어요.
My listening skills have improved a lot.
향상되다 = (an ability/quality) gets better, rises to a higher level. The thing that improves takes 이/가.
서비스 품질이 향상됐어요.
The service quality has been enhanced.
Common for skills, quality, performance, efficiency — 실력이/품질이/효율이 향상되다.
examples: 매일 연습하니까 발음이 향상됐어요.
Since I practice every day, my pronunciation has improved.
Classic study context — 발음이/문법이 향상되다.
업데이트 후 속도가 크게 향상됐습니다.
After the update, the speed greatly improved.
Formal 향상됐습니다 fits product notes and reviews.
꾸준히 운동하면 체력이 향상될 거예요.
If you exercise regularly, your stamina will improve.
체력이 향상되다 = stamina improves — natural in health/fitness advice.
nuance: 향상되다 is a 되다 verb meaning a skill, quality, or level rises and gets better — it's the intransitive, formal cousin of 좋아지다 (to get better). Use it for measurable things like 실력, 품질, 성능, 효율, 체력. To improve something on purpose, use the transitive 향상시키다 (실력을 향상시키다). Watch the contraction: 향상되어요 shortens to 향상돼요, and the past is 향상됐어요.
mistakes: Don't use it transitively — say 실력이 향상됐어요 (skills improved), but 실력을 향상시켰어요 when YOU improved them (향상시키다).
Write the polite form as 향상돼요 and the past as 향상됐어요 — not 향상되요 / 향상됬어요.

english: to decrease, to decline, to drop
usage: 인구가 매년 감소하고 있어요.
The population is decreasing every year.
감소하다 = (a number/amount) goes down. Formal, statistical word; the thing takes 이/가 (intransitive).
올해 매출이 10% 감소했어요.
Sales decreased 10% this year.
Common in business/news with figures — 매출이/수요가 ~% 감소하다.
examples: 출생률이 빠르게 감소하고 있습니다.
The birth rate is declining rapidly.
Formal 감소하고 있습니다 fits news and reports about social trends.
관광객 수가 크게 감소했어요.
The number of tourists dropped sharply.
수가 감소하다 = the count drops — pairs naturally with 크게/빠르게 (sharply/rapidly).
운동하면 스트레스가 감소할 수 있어요.
Exercising can reduce stress.
Also works for abstract things like 스트레스/위험이 감소하다.
nuance: 감소하다 is the formal, statistical verb for an amount or number going down — its opposite is 증가하다 (to increase), and the pair shows up constantly in news, reports, and graphs. In casual speech Koreans usually say 줄다 or 줄어들다 instead (손님이 줄었어요). 감소하다 is intransitive (이/가); to reduce something on purpose, use the transitive 줄이다 (비용을 줄이다) or 감소시키다.
mistakes: Don't use it transitively — say 비용이 감소했어요 (the cost decreased), but 비용을 줄였어요 when YOU cut it.
In everyday talk, 줄어들다 sounds more natural than 감소하다; save 감소하다 for numbers, reports, and formal contexts.

english: to increase, to rise, to grow
usage: 외국인 관광객이 증가하고 있어요.
The number of foreign tourists is increasing.
증가하다 = (a number/amount) goes up. Formal counterpart of 늘다; the thing takes 이/가 (intransitive).
올해 수출이 크게 증가했어요.
Exports increased significantly this year.
Business/news word, often with figures — 수출이/수요가 ~% 증가하다.
examples: 1인 가구가 빠르게 증가하고 있습니다.
Single-person households are rapidly increasing.
Formal 증가하고 있습니다 fits reports on social trends.
기온이 오르면 전기 사용량이 증가해요.
When the temperature rises, electricity usage increases.
Cause-and-effect with numbers — 사용량이/소비가 증가하다.
스마트폰 사용 시간이 매년 증가하는 추세예요.
Smartphone usage time is on an upward trend every year.
증가하는 추세 = 'an increasing trend' — a very common set phrase.
nuance: 증가하다 is the formal, statistical verb for an amount or number rising, and it pairs directly with 감소하다 (to decrease). It dominates news, reports, and data discussion. For casual everyday speech Koreans say 늘다 or 늘어나다 instead (손님이 늘었어요). It's intransitive (이/가); to increase something on purpose, use the transitive 늘리다 (시간을 늘리다) or 증가시키다.
mistakes: Don't use it transitively — say 인구가 증가했어요 (the population increased), but 인원을 늘렸어요 when YOU increased the number (늘리다).
In everyday talk, 늘어나다 sounds more natural; reserve 증가하다 for numbers, statistics, and formal contexts.

english: to maintain, to keep, to sustain
usage: 건강을 유지하려고 매일 운동해요.
I exercise every day to maintain my health.
유지하다 = to keep something in its current state. It's transitive: the thing you keep takes 을/를.
적정 온도를 유지해 주세요.
Please keep it at the right temperature.
Common with conditions and levels — 온도를/거리를/관계를 유지하다.
examples: 냉장고는 항상 일정한 온도를 유지해요.
The fridge always maintains a constant temperature.
온도를 유지하다 = keeps a steady temperature — works for machines and bodies.
좋은 성적을 유지하기가 쉽지 않아요.
It's not easy to maintain good grades.
성적을 유지하다 = keep up one's grades; ~기가 쉽지 않다 = 'it's not easy to.'
두 나라는 우호 관계를 유지하고 있습니다.
The two countries maintain a friendly relationship.
관계를 유지하다 = sustain a relationship — common in formal/news contexts.
nuance: 유지하다 means to keep something the way it is so it doesn't change or decline — health, temperature, grades, balance, relationships. It's transitive, so the thing maintained takes 을/를 (거리를 유지하다 = keep your distance). The intransitive 'be maintained / stay as is' is 유지되다 (상태가 유지되다). It carries a slightly formal tone but is common in everyday advice about health and habits.
mistakes: It's transitive — use 을/를: 건강을 유지하다, not 건강이 유지하다. For 'is maintained,' switch to 유지되다.
Don't confuse it with 유치하다 (to be childish / to attract), which looks similar but is unrelated.

english: to form, to shape, to build up
usage: 어릴 때 성격이 형성돼요.
Personality is formed in childhood.
형성하다 is transitive (성격을 형성하다), but the intransitive 형성되다 ('be formed') is just as common: 성격이 형성되다.
좋은 습관을 형성하는 것이 중요해요.
Forming good habits is important.
습관을 형성하다 = to build up habits. Abstract, written-leaning word.
examples: 새로운 관계를 형성하는 데 시간이 걸려요.
It takes time to form new relationships.
관계를 형성하다 = build up a relationship; ~는 데 시간이 걸리다 = 'it takes time to.'
이 지역은 오래전에 형성됐어요.
This area was formed long ago.
For places/layers forming naturally, the intransitive 형성되다 is standard.
여러 의견이 모여 여론을 형성합니다.
Various opinions come together to form public opinion.
여론을 형성하다 = shape public opinion — common in formal writing about society.
nuance: 형성하다 means to form or build something up over time — a personality, a habit, a relationship, a market, public opinion. It's abstract and written-leaning. The transitive 형성하다 takes 을/를, but in practice Koreans very often use the intransitive 형성되다 for things that form on their own (성격이 형성되다 = personality is formed). For concrete 'make' you'd use 만들다; 형성하다 is for gradual, structural formation.
mistakes: For something forming naturally, prefer 형성되다 (이/가): 여론이 형성됐어요, not 여론을 형성했어요 unless an agent actively shapes it.
Don't use 형성하다 for simply making an object — '밥을 형성하다' is wrong; use 만들다 for concrete things.

english: to compose, to organize, to make up
usage: 팀을 다섯 명으로 구성했어요.
I organized the team with five people.
구성하다 = to put together / make up from parts. Transitive: the whole takes 을/를, the parts take (으)로.
이 책은 세 부분으로 구성돼 있어요.
This book is made up of three parts.
Very common as the passive 구성되다: ~(으)로 구성되어 있다 = 'consists of.'
examples: 메뉴를 코스로 구성해 주세요.
Please put together the menu as a course.
~(으)로 구성하다 = arrange/organize into a form; natural for menus, programs, plans.
우리 동아리는 다양한 사람들로 구성돼 있어요.
Our club is made up of diverse people.
X(으)로 구성되어 있다 is the standard way to say 'is composed of X.'
발표 내용을 알기 쉽게 구성했습니다.
I organized the presentation content to be easy to follow.
내용을 구성하다 = structure the content — useful for work and study.
nuance: 구성하다 means to put something together out of parts — a team, a menu, a program, the content of a presentation. It's transitive (을/를 for the whole, (으)로 for the components). Most often you'll meet its passive 구성되다, especially in the set phrase X(으)로 구성되어 있다 ('consists of / is made up of X'). It's a formal, organizational word, not for casually 'making' an object.
mistakes: For 'consists of,' use the passive: A는 B로 구성되어 있어요, not A는 B를 구성해 있어요.
Mark the parts with (으)로, not 을/를: 세 명으로 구성하다 (compose of three people).

english: to apply, to put into use
usage: 할인을 적용해 주세요.
Please apply the discount.
적용하다 = to apply a rule/discount/method to something. Transitive: what you apply takes 을/를.
새 규칙을 모든 직원에게 적용해요.
We apply the new rule to all employees.
~에/에게 적용하다 = apply TO (a target): 모든 직원에게, 이 경우에.
examples: 이 쿠폰은 온라인에만 적용돼요.
This coupon only applies online.
The passive 적용되다 ('be applied / apply') is very common for rules and discounts.
배운 내용을 실제로 적용해 보세요.
Try actually applying what you learned.
내용을/이론을 적용하다 = put knowledge into practice — common study advice.
변경된 요금은 다음 달부터 적용됩니다.
The changed fee applies from next month.
다음 달부터 적용되다 = takes effect from next month — standard notice wording.
nuance: 적용하다 means to apply a rule, discount, theory, or method so it actually takes effect — the thing applied takes 을/를, and the target takes 에/에게. You'll constantly meet the passive 적용되다 ('is applied / applies / takes effect'), as in 할인이 적용돼요 or 다음 달부터 적용됩니다. Don't confuse it with 적응하다 (to adjust/adapt to a new environment), which is one syllable different and intransitive.
mistakes: Don't mix up 적용하다 (apply a rule) with 적응하다 (adapt) — 새 회사에 적응했어요 (adapted) vs 새 규칙을 적용했어요 (applied).
Mark the target with 에/에게: 모든 경우에 적용하다, not 모든 경우를 적용하다 (을/를 marks the rule itself).

english: to carry out, to conduct, to implement
usage: 설문 조사를 실시했어요.
We conducted a survey.
실시하다 = to officially carry out a plan/policy/test. Transitive: the activity takes 을/를. Formal.
다음 주에 안전 교육을 실시합니다.
We will conduct safety training next week.
Common with organized events — 교육을/검사를/조사를/정책을 실시하다.
examples: 정부가 새 정책을 실시했습니다.
The government implemented a new policy.
정책을 실시하다 = put a policy into effect — typical news/official wording.
매년 건강 검진을 실시해요.
We carry out health checkups every year.
검진을/점검을 실시하다 = conduct checkups/inspections — organizational tone.
공사가 다음 달부터 실시될 예정입니다.
The construction is scheduled to be carried out from next month.
The passive 실시되다 ('be carried out') is common in formal announcements.
nuance: 실시하다 means to officially carry out or put into effect a planned activity — a survey, training, an exam, a policy, an inspection. It's formal and organizational, used by governments, companies, and schools, not for personal everyday actions. It's transitive (을/를), and the passive 실시되다 ('is carried out / takes effect') is frequent in notices. For just 'doing' something casually, use 하다; reserve 실시하다 for official, scheduled undertakings.
mistakes: Don't use it for personal tasks — 'I did my homework' is 숙제를 했어요, not 숙제를 실시했어요.
It's transitive — say 조사를 실시했어요; for 'was carried out,' use 실시되다 (조사가 실시됐어요).

english: to solve, to resolve, to settle
usage: 문제를 빨리 해결해야 해요.
We need to solve the problem quickly.
해결하다 = to solve/settle a problem. Transitive: the problem takes 을/를.
그 일은 잘 해결됐어요.
That matter got resolved well.
The passive 해결되다 ('be solved / work out') is very common: 문제가 해결되다.
examples: 이 앱으로 대부분의 문제를 해결할 수 있어요.
You can solve most problems with this app.
문제를 해결하다 is the core collocation — 'solve a problem.'
갈등을 대화로 해결했어요.
We resolved the conflict through dialogue.
갈등을 해결하다 = settle a conflict; 대화로 = 'through conversation.'
걱정 마세요, 제가 해결할게요.
Don't worry, I'll take care of it.
제가 해결할게요 = 'I'll handle it' — a confident, reassuring everyday line.
nuance: 해결하다 is the everyday and formal verb for solving or settling a problem, conflict, or issue — by far its most common partner is 문제 (문제를 해결하다). It's transitive (을/를). The passive 해결되다 means a matter gets resolved or works out (문제가 해결됐어요). Unlike 풀다 (which also means 'solve' for puzzles/math), 해결하다 covers problems, disputes, and situations broadly.
mistakes: It's transitive — say 문제를 해결했어요, not 문제가 해결했어요 (for 'the problem was solved,' use 해결됐어요).
For math problems or riddles specifically, 풀다 is also natural (문제를 풀다); 해결하다 suits real-life issues and disputes.

english: to take up, to occupy, to account for
usage: 식비가 생활비의 절반을 차지해요.
Food costs take up half of my living expenses.
차지하다 = to take up a portion/proportion. Transitive: the share taken takes 을/를.
우리 팀이 1위를 차지했어요.
Our team took first place.
Also 'to win/secure (a rank, a spot)': 1위를/우승을 차지하다.
examples: 주거비가 지출에서 큰 부분을 차지해요.
Housing costs make up a large part of spending.
큰 부분을 차지하다 = account for a large share — common in budget talk.
그 가수가 1위를 차지했어요.
That singer took the number one spot.
For rankings and charts — 1위를/정상을 차지하다 (take first place / the top).
짐이 자리를 너무 많이 차지해요.
The luggage takes up too much space.
자리를 차지하다 = take up space/a seat — literal, everyday use too.
nuance: 차지하다 has two everyday senses: to take up a proportion or amount (식비가 절반을 차지하다 = food is half the cost) and to secure or win something (1위를 차지하다 = take first place). It's transitive — the share or prize taken takes 을/를. The first sense is great for talking about budgets and statistics ('X accounts for Y%'); the second is common in sports, charts, and competitions.
mistakes: It's transitive — mark the share/rank with 을/를: 절반을 차지하다, 1위를 차지하다.
Don't confuse the 'win a rank' sense with 이기다 (to beat an opponent); 차지하다 is about securing the position/share itself.
